subject: On-prem arrangement: fee structure, support tiers, and migration credits
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datawave.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@datawave.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem pricing: platform fee, support tiers, and migration credits

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As discussed, DataWave is evaluating an on-prem (VPC) deployment of Redwood for our analytics inference workloads. A few clarifying questions so we can model costs for our FY27 budget: 

- How do you define the "platform fee" vs licensing for on-prem? Is the platform fee a fixed annual charge or scaled to committed throughput?
- We have ~40 inference GPUs today, growing to ~120 over 12 months — do you offer step-up pricing or volume discounts for reserved capacity?
- Support tiers: what’s included in Standard vs Premier (response SLOs, RPO for backups, on-call)?
- Any migration/onboarding credits for customers moving from self-hosted solutions (we'll likely need an SOW for two weeks of delivery support).

I attached a high-level infra spreadsheet (DataWave_Infra.xlsx) that shows our current nodes and expected growth. We are targeting a Q3 piloted deployment and would like a ballpark committed-annual pricing + concessions to present to procurement.

Appreciate any examples/benchmarks you can share.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering
DataWave Analytics
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datawave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem pricing: platform fee, support tiers, and migration credits

Hi Samir — thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear breakdown. Below is a concise way we usually structure on-prem (VPC) engagements; I’ll loop in Marcus (pricing) and Laura (delivery) for any specifics on SOW.

Option A — Committed Annual (recommended for predictable TCO)
- Platform fee: fixed annual platform fee that covers control plane, console, model catalog updates, and telemetry (applies regardless of nodes).
- Licensing: per-GPU seat fee for dedicated runtime; discounted tiers at 50 and 100+ GPU commits.
- Support: Standard (8x5, 24h response), Premier (24x7 with 4h response, on-call escalation), Professional Services billed separately or packaged as a migration credit with commit.

Option B — Metered + Lower Platform Fee
- Smaller fixed platform fee + metered per-token/throughput billing. Better if your capacity is variable.

Concessions we can consider for a Q3 pilot: a migration credit (applied against first-year platform fee) and 10–15% off list for a first-year commit at 100+ GPUs. If you’re willing to sign a 12-month commit at a 100-GPU baseline, we can do a structured credit for SOW hours and reduced platform fee in year 1.

I’ve attached a short fee sheet with tier examples and a draft SOW. Can you confirm whether DataWave prefers an annual invoiced commit or quarterly billing? Also, are there specific SOC2 / audit evidence items you’ll need up-front?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Redwood_OnPrem_Tiered_Fee_Sheet.pdf attached]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: On-prem pricing: platform fee, support tiers, and migration credits (internal)

Team — forwarding Samir's ask. Key asks to negotiate: 100+ GPU discount and a migration credit for SOW. He prefers an annual commit but open to quarterly invoicing if it lowers start-of-year cash impact.

My thinking: we should protect ASP (platform fee) but be flexible on year-1 reductions tied to commit and timing. Suggestion: 12-month commitment at a 100-GPU baseline, 12% off list platform fee for year 1 + $40k migration credit (applied as a one-time invoice credit) and Premier trial for first 30 days. If they want quarterly invoicing, increase platform fee by 6% to cover cash risk.

Questions for Marcus: does 12% + $40k credit fit within our discount playbook for mid-market enterprise?
For Laura: does Delivery have capacity to include the 2-week SOW + 1 week of runbook handover in the migration credit?

Thanks,
Grace
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: On-prem pricing: platform fee, support tiers, and migration credits (internal)

Grace — high-level: 12% + $40k credit is reasonable for a 100-GPU anchor if they commit to 12 months and accept DocuSign + PO within 30 days. A couple tactical notes: 

- Make the migration credit conditional on signing a short SOW milestone acceptance (so we get closure on deliverables).
- If they insist on quarterly billing, add a 6–8% lift or require a one-time start-up invoice to cover the platform fee for the first quarter up-front.
- Premier trial: allow 30 days, then auto-convert to Standard unless they explicitly choose Premier and we invoice the delta.

Also recommend we insert a cap on on-prem license upward-scaling commitment: allow them to add GPUs mid-year at a pro-rated list with a 5% commit discount for any incremental purchase above 20 GPUs. That protects pricing and lets them scale predictably.

If Legal is going to ask about audit logs/SOC evidence, we should commit to providing our standard SOC2 package and a short implementation runbook for any on-prem logging connectors. Laura — can Delivery commit to a 3-week window for runbook delivery after the pilot ends?

If all that looks good I’ll bless the concession in HubSpot and we can prepare the SOW + DocuSign link.

— Marcus
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datawave.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@datawave.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal: committed-annual on-prem package (100 GPU baseline)

Hi Samir — following internal alignment, please find our formal proposal summary below and attached documents. This is intentionally tight so procurement can model the numbers.

Summary (100-GPU baseline, 12-month commit)
- Year 1 platform fee (net): list platform fee less 12% = $360,000 net (applies to control plane, console, model updates, telemetry).
- Licensing: per-GPU runtime license, list $7,000/GPU/year; with 100-GPU baseline we apply 10% off list -> $6,300/GPU/year.
- Migration credit: one-time $40,000 credit applied to first-year invoice; contingent on SOW milestone acceptance (deliverables: 2-week onboarding, runbook, handover).
- Support: 30-day Premier trial included; after trial, Standard included. Premier optional add-on for 24x7 4h response at additional fee (see attached sheet).
- Billing: annual invoicing preferred. If you require quarterly invoicing, a 6% uplift on the platform fee will apply to offset cash timing.
- Scale flexibility: pro-rated add-on pricing for GPUs added mid-term; incremental commits >20 GPUs receive a 5% discount.

Attachments: Redwood_OnPrem_Tiered_Fee_Sheet.pdf, Redwood_SOW-Draft.docx
Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7654321 ; DocuSign (proposal): https://www.docusign.com/REDWOOD-DW-048

Next steps: we can generate a DocuSign for the commercial term sheet and a short SOW. If this looks good I’ll send the documents to you and procurement; Marcus will trigger the discount in our deal system. Please let me know if procurement prefers a PO or a DocuSign signature flow.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Grace — appreciate the clear proposal. This aligns with what procurement was hoping to see. A few quick clarifying points before we route to legal/finance: 

1) Can the $40k migration credit be shown as a line-item credit on the initial invoice?
2) We will take the annual invoicing option (no uplift) if we can commit to executing within 30 days — otherwise we’ll revert to quarterly and accept the uplift.
3) Please include the SOC2 package link and a short log-forwarding runbook in the SOW.

If you can send DocuSign + SOW with the credit visible as a credit line (and the SOC2 bundle link), we’ll push to issue a PO the same week.

Thanks — Samir
VP Engineering
DataWave Analytics
